Diffuse

dih-FYOOZ -- verb stress on the second syllable (the related adjective, meaning 'spread out,' is pronounced dih-FYOOSS). · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To diffuse is to spread out over a wide area.

Scientists watched as the colored dye began to diffuse through the still water in the tank.

Worked Example

A single drop of perfume released near an open window slowly makes its scent noticeable throughout an entire room within a few minutes.

That gradual spreading out from one point to fill a wider space is exactly what it means to diffuse. Unlike 'concentrate,' which gathers something into one place, diffuse spreads it out.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

spread: to extend over a wider area

disperse: to scatter over a wide area

scatter: to distribute widely in different directions

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

concentrate: to gather something into one place

condense: to make something more compact or concentrated

Where it sits · how quickly and completely things scatter — spread → diffuse → disperse

spread vs. diffuse: Spread is a simple, everyday word close to diffuse -- diffuse often appears in more scientific contexts, like gases or liquids, while spread is used far more broadly for anything expanding outward.

disperse vs. diffuse: Disperse can feel more formal than diffuse: diffuse usually describes a gradual, gentle spreading, while disperse can describe something scattering more quickly and completely in different directions.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dif-

Prefix — dif-: apart, in different directions (the form dis- takes before f) (Latin)

Root — fuse

Root — fuse: to pour (from Latin fundere, 'to pour'; its stem fus- -- the same root in infuse and refund)

Put it together

Put it together: Dif- ('apart' -- the shape dis- takes before f) + fuse ('to pour', from Latin fundere) spell diffuse. To diffuse something, at its root, is to pour it outward in different directions until it spreads through a wider space -- the same root that gives us infuse and refund.

Use the root in a new word: infuse

Use the root in a new word: infuse: The chef let the tea leaves infuse the hot water for exactly five minutes before serving.

Root Check

Word Choice

As a verb, diffuse describes something spreading gradually through a space, often gas, liquid, or light; the related adjective 'diffuse' (a different pronunciation) describes something already spread out, as in 'diffuse light.'
